visual_checkpoints.note: The paddle sits low near the waist with the tip pointing down.
Mostly a shoulder lift with only a small wrist movement.

summary: Your dink comes from a nice low, stable base, and your chest stays up through the shot. The main thing to fix is where your paddle waits between shots: it hangs low, so you are late on fast balls. Keep the paddle up in front of your chest and shorten your backswing.

strengths.title: Chest stays up
strengths.detail: You bend your knees instead of folding at the waist. That keeps your eyes level and your dinks consistent.

evidence.observation: Your chest stays upright while your knees do the bending.

strengths.title: Smooth shoulder lift
strengths.detail: The dink comes from your shoulder, not a wrist flick. That keeps the paddle face steady.

evidence.observation: The paddle face stays steady as you lift through the ball.

weaknesses.title: Paddle hangs low between shots
weaknesses.detail: While you wait for the ball, your paddle drops to knee height. Fast balls at your body then catch you late.
weaknesses.why_it_matters: A paddle held up in front saves time and lets you block hard shots at the kitchen.

evidence.observation: In the ready position the paddle hangs by your knee.

weaknesses.title: Backswing too big for a dink
weaknesses.detail: You take the paddle back further than a dink needs. A big swing makes the ball pop up.
weaknesses.why_it_matters: A short swing keeps your dinks low and hard to attack.

evidence.observation: The paddle travels well behind your hip before contact.

improvements.title: Keep the paddle up and in front
improvements.how_to_fix: After every shot, bring the paddle back up in front of your chest. Hold it there with the tip up.
improvements.goal: Paddle at chest height between shots.

improvements.title: Shorten the backswing
improvements.how_to_fix: Start the dink with the paddle already in front. Lift the ball with your shoulder instead of swinging.
improvements.goal: Paddle stays in front of your body on the dink.

safety_notes.message: Long dink sessions in a low stance load your knees; take short breaks.

not_assessable.how_to_capture: Film from behind the baseline so the kitchen is in view.

recording_tips: Keep the phone steady at hip height.
Record at least six dinks in a row.
